root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: o.string == &algo at the first rollback 'S' cleanup after the leading 'b' output has already been replayed from ap_copy
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When rollback reaches the first successful 'S' result of the failing bSS parse, the source-level slot recovered by `o.string = va_arg(ap_copy, ssh_string *)` must be the earlier successful `&algo` argument, which requires the copied va_list to have already advanced past the leading scalar `&has_sign` slot even though `buffer->secure` is false.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original keeps `va_arg(ap_copy, uint8_t *)` under `if (buffer->secure)` in the rollback `b` case, so ordinary packet buffers leave ap_copy positioned on `&has_sign`. The fixed original advances past the scalar slot unconditionally, so the later `S` cleanup recovers `&algo` and the protected SAFE_FREE executes on the intended ssh_string slot instead of retyping the caller's one-byte flag as `ssh_string *`.

nodes.state: SAFE_FREE dereferences the same misaligned ssh_string slot chosen by rollback, so the sink reads through the caller's `has_sign` stack byte instead of the intended `algo` slot.
The first rollback `S` cleanup recovers `o.string = &has_sign` instead of `&algo`, retyping the caller's one-byte flag slot as `ssh_string *`.

The publickey-specific `ssh_buffer_unpack(packet, "bSS", ...)` call passes `&has_sign` as the first output slot for the leading `b` and `&algo` as the next successful `S` slot that rollback is supposed to revisit.

edges.relation: The misaligned ssh_string slot selected by `va_arg(ap_copy, ssh_string *)` is the same slot SAFE_FREE dereferences four lines later.
The stale first variadic output slot `&has_sign` is recovered as `o.string` when rollback enters the first `S` cleanup.
